items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: You know I mean there are some people that think Tommy Dorsey was the greatest ever and as a balladeer for that style of playing that he kind of evolved from listening to Lawrence Brown.

ctx.x: You sound like a modest man as far as how you think about your own playing. And if you could set that modesty aside for a moment, where do you think you fall in the list of influential trombone players?

It’s not for me to say. Everybody has a different take. You know I mean there are some people that think Tommy Dorsey was the greatest ever and as a balladeer for that style of playing that he kind of evolved from listening to Lawrence Brown. He’s got Lawrence Brown. Because Lawrence Brown used many types of vibrato. Sometimes he’d use a lip vibrato, sometimes he’d use a slide vibrato. And they used to run up to the Cotton Club to see Duke and all that and caught that ball and ran with it and made it his whole…
going back to 1970. And of course the shells. I brought that to jazz [inaudible]. People can judge it how they want. That’s not my care. I don’t really care, it’s not why I’m doing it.
